claims.statement: The register structure is legally specified in Commission Implementing Regulation 2024/2956 and supported by an official EBA data model and reporting package.
The official EBA materials are a free substitute for software-only generation and validation features.
Data quality was difficult in the 2024 dry run: 6.5% of registers passed every check and half of the rest failed fewer than five of 116 checks.
Poland had a concrete 2025 remediation event in which entities with an EBA-rejected SPR-PF-18 had to resubmit using the latest KNF form.
Continued KNF training in 2026 indicates that accurate SPR-PF-18 preparation remains an operational concern, but it does not quantify commercial demand.
A Polish product must fit KNF's SSD and SPR-PF-18 workflow, not merely produce a generic EBA-shaped dataset.
The competitive set already includes enterprise GRC functionality and a small-entity product with public annual pricing from EUR 1,500 to EUR 12,500.
Price above the public specialist range is plausible only if private deployment, contract lineage or remediation services produce measurable incremental value.

No public evidence reviewed establishes target-customer willingness to buy, advisor channel commitment, acceptable security architecture, sales-cycle length or achievable margins for this proposed entrant.

contrary_evidence: Official EBA and KNF tools, forms, examples and training let entities remediate without a new vendor.
ServiceNow already manages DORA register records and a DORA-native competitor publicly undercuts the original annual pricing hypothesis.
A one-time first-reporting rejection wave may decline as internal teams learn the process.
The evidence shows reporting friction, not a count of paying customers or budget ownership.
Financial-sector security review and contract-data sensitivity may prevent a part-time new entrant from accessing production data.
